'''Bärbel Hönisch''' (born 1974) is a German [[Paleoceanography|paleoceanographer]] and [[Paleoclimatology|paleoclimatologist]], author, and professor at [[Columbia University]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name="ldeo-cv">{{cite web|title=Curriculum vitae: Dr. Bärbel Hönisch|periodical=|publisher=Columbia University|url=https://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/sites/default/files/H%C3%B6nisch%20CV%202020.pdf|format=|access-date=9 January 2020|last=|date=2020|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref>

== Education ==
Hönisch earned a [[vordiplom]] in biology at [[Bielefeld University]] in 1995, a diplom ([[master's degree]]) in marine biology in 1999 at the [[University of Bremen]], and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in natural sciences in 2002 at the [[Alfred Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research]].<ref name="col-hoe-home">{{cite web|title=Bärbel Hönisch|periodical=|publisher=Columbia University|url=https://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/~hoenisch/home.html|access-date=9 January 2020|last=|date=|year=|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
From 2002 to 2006 she worked in various scientific roles, including at the [[Lamont–Doherty Earth Observatory]], and since 2007 she has been a professor at Columbia University. She has been a tenured professor at the Department of Earth & Environmental Sciences there since 2019.<ref name="ldeo-cv" />

Based on an analysis of the Middle [[Pleistocene]], in the course of which the duration of the various [[glacial period]]s increased from 40,000 to 100,000 years, Hoenisch and her co-authors reconstructed the temperature fluctuations and the carbon dioxide concentration over the past 2.1 million years in a study published in 2009 indicating that the current [[Carbon dioxide|CO<sub>2</sub>]] values are the highest within this comparison period.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hönisch|first1=Bärbel|last2=Hemming|first2=N. Gary|last3=Archer|first3=David|last4=Siddall|first4=Mark|last5=McManus|first5=Jerry F.|date=19 June 2009|title=Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Concentration Across the Mid-Pleistocene Transition|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1171477|journal=Science|language=en|volume=324|issue=5934|pages=1551–1554|doi=10.1126/science.1171477|issn=0036-8075|pmid=19541994|bibcode=2009Sci...324.1551H|s2cid=206518823|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

She was the lead author of a 2012 study on [[ocean acidification]] in [[Science (journal)|Science]], collaborating with [[James Zachos]], [[Ellen Thomas (scientist)|Ellen Thomas]], and others. Summarizing the results, she said, "What we’re doing today really stands out. We know that life during past ocean acidification events was not wiped out—new species evolved to replace those that died off. But if industrial carbon emissions continue at the current pace, we may lose organisms we care about—coral reefs, oysters, salmon."<ref>{{cite web|title=Ocean Acidification Rate May Be Unprecedented, Study Says|periodical=|publisher=Columbia University|url=https://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/news-events/ocean-acidification-rate-may-be-unprecedented-study-says|format=|access-date=9 January 2020|last=|date=1 March 2012|language=|pages=|quote=|archive-date=27 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191227023515/https://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/news-events/ocean-acidification-rate-may-be-unprecedented-study-says|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hönisch received the 2018 Willi Dansgaard Award from the [[American Geophysical Union]] in recognition of her "research impact, innovative interdisciplinary work, educational accomplishments (mentoring), societal impact, or other relevant contributions and to acknowledge that the awardee shows exceptional promise for continued leadership in paleoceanography or paleoclimatology." The award cited her pioneering work in the development and application of geochemical [[Proxy (climate)|proxies]] for reconstruction of paleo ocean temperatures, carbonate chemistry, and atmospheric CO<sub>2</sub>.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=16 November 2018|title=Hönisch Receives 2018 Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology Willi Dansgaard Award|url=https://eos.org/agu-news/honisch-receives-2018-paleoceanography-and-paleoclimatology-willi-dansgaard-award|access-date=7 April 2021|journal=Eos|volume=99 |language=en-US|doi=10.1029/2018EO110103|s2cid=239785535|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2018 she gave the Marie-Tharp Lecture at [[GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel|GEOMAR]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=23 March 2018|title=Dem Klimawandel auf der Spur|trans-title=On the trail of climate change|url=https://www.geomar.de/de/news/article/dem-klimawandel-auf-der-spur/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116083619/https://www.geomar.de/de/news/article/dem-klimawandel-auf-der-spur/|archive-date=16 January 2020|website=GEOMAR Helmholtz-Zentrum für Ozeanforschung Kiel}}</ref>

[[Web of Science]] records 60 publications and an [[H-index|h-Index]] of 27 (as of January 2020).<ref>Query of the [[Web of Science]] database on 17 January 2020.</ref>
